checkpoints: A single edit schedules no immediate store write; exactly one write occurs after 120 ms without another edit.
Multiple edits within one 120 ms burst produce one write containing only the latest text.
After one burst saves, a later burst schedules and saves normally.
Edits for different document identities use their respective coordinator-owned trailing tasks.
Opening another document, closing the view, or disposing the workspace does not incorrectly transfer or cancel a document buffer’s pending save.
A synchronous navigation initiated by a store listener during a delayed save leaves view identity, subscription cleanup, and later saves consistent.
Search preview still uses its independent 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation behavior.
Public JavaScript and Vue sources continue to parse/build after the maintenance change.
forbidden_effects: Do not write workspace edits to the store on every keystroke.
Do not save an earlier value from a burst after a later value has been entered.
Do not make a trailing task single-use; later bursts must still save.
Do not move document-buffer ownership from the coordinator dictionary to the current view or Badge subscription.
Do not cancel a document’s pending save merely because its view is retired, closed, replaced, or disposed.
Do not alter createWorkspace/open/edit/close/dispose public interfaces or source identity, text, event, revision, and status payload semantics.
Do not change the adjacent search preview, its 40 ms quiet interval, or its transient ownership behavior.
Do not weaken synchronous reentrant-navigation handling around view retirement, store writes, subscriptions, or rendering.
lifecycle_identity: Each document id identifies one persistent trailing edit buffer in the coordinator dictionary.

The current view object contains the active document id, its coordinator-owned buffer, and the live store-subscription stop callback; retiring the view removes the badge subscription but does not own or destroy the document buffer.
Search preview has a separate transient trailing task and is not part of document-buffer lifecycle.
The request counter identifies the latest navigation request so synchronous reentry can invalidate an older open operation.

obligations.text: When edit(text) is called with a current view, enqueue text through that view’s existing document-specific trailing task instead of writing directly to the store.
For edits belonging to one burst, wait for a 120 ms quiet interval and then perform one store write using only the latest text.
After a burst flushes, the same document buffer must accept and save subsequent bursts.
Document trailing tasks must remain keyed and owned by the coordinator dictionary so buffer lifetime is independent of the current view badge and its subscription.
Preserve open, close, dispose, rendering, subscription, store event, and synchronous navigation behavior except for the requested delayed/coalesced timing of edit writes.
Leave createSearchPreview and its separate 40 ms trailing task unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Each edit updates the pending latest value and resets the document task’s 120 ms timer.
The delayed task retires its timer state before invoking store.write, allowing synchronous callbacks and later pushes to establish a fresh burst safely.
View retirement clears the published view and stops its live subscription independently of any pending document-buffer task.
An open request must remain invalidatable after callback-capable retirement work and before publishing the newly opened view.
The store write synchronously publishes its event to currently registered listeners; any navigation they initiate must be handled as synchronous reentry.
preservation: Preserve the public workspace methods open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose().
Preserve store read/write/subscribe synchronous behavior and original event payload semantics.
Preserve rendering of null during retirement and rendering of the opened document using the store’s current text.
Preserve removal of the old view’s live store subscription when retiring it.
Preserve the request-generation guard that prevents a stale open from continuing after synchronous navigation.
Preserve document buffers across view changes because they are coordinator-owned rather than Badge-owned.
Preserve search-preview query coalescing and hide cancellation exactly as adjacent behavior outside this change.
scope: Change only workspace draft-edit persistence behavior in src/coordinator.js: route current-view edits through the already-created per-document 120 ms trailing buffer.
The existing generic trailing-task implementation in src/services.js is normative reusable behavior unless a business-code correction is strictly necessary to meet the task.
src/Workspace.vue public component methods and lifecycle remain in scope for preservation, not redesign.
createSearchPreview in src/services.js is explicitly out of scope.

Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst.
Subsequent bursts must continue to save.
Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.
A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge.
Save callbacks can synchronously navigate.
Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval.
Document-buffer responsibility: coordinator dictionary
createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide().
Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.
Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription.
A store listener may call navigation synchronously.
All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
if(!resources.has(id))resources.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)))
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));

triggers: Calling edit(text) while a current document view exists starts or resets that document’s trailing 120 ms save interval.
Expiration of 120 ms with no newer edit flushes the latest pending text to store.write for that document id.
A new edit after a completed flush begins a new independent burst.
open(id), close(), and dispose() retire the current view/subscription but do not redefine document-buffer ownership.
A delayed store write synchronously notifies store listeners, which may synchronously initiate navigation.

The public documents do not specify error handling when timer, store, subscription, or rendering callbacks throw; do not introduce new semantics without evidence.
The public documents do not prescribe deletion or final flushing of coordinator dictionary entries; preserve their existing lifetime.
